chapter: Old New Orleans bands and Buddy Bolden
title: Clarinets in string bands, and switching between A, B-flat and C
summary: Bands used different clarinets per key, but Lorenzo, Picou and the uncle used one B-flat clarinet and adjusted the pitch by pulling the barrel.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I'd like to come back to the Boling Band just for a moment. You said they had a clarinet in the band. I wonder how, was there any difference in those clarinets, in those string bands, for instance, in there would be in a, we'll say like a brass band or in a more classical band. classical band, would there be any different way of blowing it?

Well I'll tell you, there's some band that used to, some kind of play used to use a B flat and A, some used to use C clarinet, and they used to change up in between when playing, you know. If they played a certain number and was written in A, well he picked up his A clarinet. He picked up B flat, he picked up B flat clarinet, you understand? It wasn't C, he got his C clarinet. You understand? That's how it was done. Now a lot of fellas like Picoon and my brother and my uncle and them, they didn't need that. You could use that B flat clarinet on it. You didn't need that clarinet.
Sometimes they had to pull it out the shank, out the tune, and sometimes they'd transport it.

That's right. You could just reach up there and catch the naked, squeeze it up a little bit, pull it out, or push it in. That's the difference there was in that. And if you're using the B flat clarinet, because you had to play that A and C, D, well that's a D-partone clarinet, all together.
